To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

concrete shear strength and the corresponding shear strength components are significantly reduced by sulfate attack, and that shear dilation is diminished while friction component has a small increase at the early sulfate exposure period.

shear dilation of concrete diminishes, friction component of shear strength has a slight increase in the early sulfate exposure period and rapid decrease in the later sulfate exposure period and the failure criterion of the concrete specimens is transformed from bi linear Mohr-Coulomb (MC) criterion before exposure to the MC criterion after exposure in the sulfate solutions.

the shear strength of concrete is significantly reduced by the external sulfate attack, and the failure criterion of the concrete is transformed from the bi-linear Mohr-Coulomb criterion before exposure to the liner Mohr-Coulom criterion after exposure in the sulfate solutions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the change of shear strength and its component of concrete under sulfate attack, which is an important aspect of concrete behavior under sulfate attack.

the time dependent evolution and deterioration mechanisms of the shear strength and shear strength components of concrete under sulfate exposure conditions, which will provide a deeper insight into the shear behavior of sulfate attacked concrete.
the shear strength and failure criterion of concrete under direct shearing in sulfate solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the time dependent evolution on shear strength and its corresponding components of concrete fully immersed sulfate solutions is a complex phenomenon, and the deterioration of concrete under ESA is a multi-mechanism process.
the shear strength of concrete immersed in sulfate solution is time-dependent and decreases over sulfate exposure period.

the shear strength of concrete is reduced due to sulfate attack, and the shear strength of the concrete is reduced due the reduction in the friction component, the shear dilation, the shear strength of aggregate and the shear strength at the interface between cement paste and aggregate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shear strength of concrete immersed in sulfate solutions decreases over time.
the shear strength of concrete specimens subjected to direct shearing is significantly influenced by sulfate attack.

the deterioration of concrete shear strength is mainly caused by the reduction of concrete cohesion and friction, which can be attributed to the reduction of interfacial transition zone (ITZ) strength and the formation of gypsum crystals on concrete surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shear strength and its component of concrete specimens under sulfate attack are significantly influenced by sulfate exposure time and w/b ratios.
the shear behavior of concrete under direct shearing is significantly influenced by ESA, where the shear dilation of concrete diminishes over exposure period in sulfate solution.
shear strength of concrete specimens under sulfate exposure is not only a function of w/b ratio, but also of sulfate attack exposure period.
